desc:
A sensor reports readings over time. events[i] = [time, value], and the times are given in non-decreasing order (several readings can share one time). After each event arrives at time t, look at the recent window: all events so far whose time is greater than t - span (so times in (t - span, t], the new event included).

For every event, report twice the median of the values in its recent window. The median of an even count is the average of the two middle values, so doubling keeps everything an integer.

events = [[1,5], [2,1], [4,9], [5,3], [9,7]], span = 3
t=1: window {5}        -> 10
t=2: window {5, 1}     -> 1 + 5 = 6
t=4: times 2..4 {1, 9} -> 10
t=5: times 3..5 {9, 3} -> 12
t=9: times 7..9 {7}    -> 14
answer = [10, 6, 10, 12, 14]
hints: Events leave the window in the same order in which they arrived, because times never decrease. A pointer to the oldest live event is enough to know what to expire.
Two heaps (lower half and upper half) give the median of a growing set. Removing a specific element from the middle of a heap is the problem.
Use lazy deletion: remember that an event expired, but only physically pop it when it reaches the top of its heap. Track the number of live elements per heap separately to decide when to rebalance.
editorial: Combine two ideas. First, the two-heap median: a max-heap lo with the smaller half and a min-heap hi with the larger half, lo holding the extra element for odd counts. Second, lazy deletion: heaps cannot delete arbitrary elements cheaply, so when an event expires we mark its id as dead, decrease the live count of the heap it belongs to, and only discard the stale entry when it floats to the top.

For each new event, first expire every old event with time ≤ t - span (a queue pointer walks over them), then insert the new value on the correct side, then rebalance using the live counts. Before reading a root or comparing against it, clean dead entries off the top of that heap. Which heap an element lives in is recorded when it is inserted or moved.

Every event is pushed, moved and popped a constant number of times at O(log n) each, so the time is O(n log n); space is O(n). A sorted list rebuilt per event would be O(n<sup>2</sup> log n) in the worst case.
solution:
import heapq


class TwoHeaps:
    """lo = max-heap of the lower half (size = size of hi, or one more), hi = min-heap of the upper half."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.lo, self.hi = [], []          # entries (-value, id) and (value, id)
        self.dead = set()                  # ids removed but still sitting inside a heap
        self.side = {}                     # id -> 0 (in lo) or 1 (in hi)
        self.nlo = self.nhi = 0            # live sizes
        self.slo = self.shi = 0            # live sums

    def _clean(self, h):
        while h and h[0][1] in self.dead:
            self.dead.discard(heapq.heappop(h)[1])

    def add(self, i, x):
        self._clean(self.lo)
        if self.nlo == 0 or x <= -self.lo[0][0]:
            heapq.heappush(self.lo, (-x, i))
            self.side[i] = 0
            self.nlo += 1
            self.slo += x
        else:
            heapq.heappush(self.hi, (x, i))
            self.side[i] = 1
            self.nhi += 1
            self.shi += x
        self._balance()

    def remove(self, i, x):
        if self.side.pop(i) == 0:
            self.nlo -= 1
            self.slo -= x
        else:
            self.nhi -= 1
            self.shi -= x
        self.dead.add(i)
        self._balance()

    def _balance(self):
        while self.nlo > self.nhi + 1:
            self._clean(self.lo)
            nx, i = heapq.heappop(self.lo)
            heapq.heappush(self.hi, (-nx, i))
            self.side[i] = 1
            self.nlo -= 1
            self.nhi += 1
            self.slo += nx
            self.shi -= nx
        while self.nhi > self.nlo:
            self._clean(self.hi)
            x, i = heapq.heappop(self.hi)
            heapq.heappush(self.lo, (-x, i))
            self.side[i] = 0
            self.nhi -= 1
            self.nlo += 1
            self.shi -= x
            self.slo += x

    def median2(self):
        """Twice the median of the live values."""
        self._clean(self.lo)
        if self.nlo > self.nhi:
            return -2 * self.lo[0][0]
        self._clean(self.hi)
        return -self.lo[0][0] + self.hi[0][0]

    def cost(self):
        """Minimum total |x - c| over the live values."""
        self._clean(self.lo)
        med = -self.lo[0][0]
        return self.shi - self.slo + (self.nlo - self.nhi) * med


def recentMedians(events, span):
    t = TwoHeaps()
    out = []
    old = 0
    for i, (time, value) in enumerate(events):
        while events[old][0] <= time - span:
            t.remove(old, events[old][1])
            old += 1
        t.add(i, value)
        out.append(t.median2())
    return out
